title: The integral constructible category is O_E-linear with O_E-linear shift
statement: Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $Y$. The derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ of sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] is $\mathcal O_E$-linear: $a\in\mathcal O_E$ acts on every Hom group through the ring map $\mathcal O_E=\varprojlim_n A_{E,n}\to\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$ induced by the constant sections, composition is $\mathcal O_E$-bilinear, and the shift functors act $\mathcal O_E$-linearly. Consequently the full subcategory $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], with the triangulated structure of [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated], is an $\mathcal O_E$-linear triangulated category with $\mathcal O_E$-linear shift.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules to the free rank-one module $M=\mathcal O_E$. Its finite-generation hypothesis holds because $1$ generates $M$. It identifies the canonical reduction map $\mathcal O_E\to\varprojlim_n A_{E,n}$ with an isomorphism. This is a ring isomorphism, since each coordinate is the quotient ring homomorphism and addition and multiplication of compatible sequences are coordinatewise.

proof.text: For each object $U$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, map $a\in\mathcal O_E$ to the sequence of constant sections $(a\bmod\varpi_E^n)_U$ in $(A_{E,n})_Y(U)$. These sections come from the constant-presheaf-to-sheaf map in the definition of $(A_{E,n})_Y$. The reduction maps take the $(n+1)$st coordinate to the $n$th. The sectionwise inverse-limit description therefore gives an element $c_U(a)$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}(U)$. Coordinatewise ring operations make $c_U$ a unital ring homomorphism, and restriction along $V\to U$ takes $c_U(a)$ to $c_V(a)$. At the terminal object $Y$ this is precisely the stated map to global sections, using the identification of Step 1. No equality between the constant sheaf $(\mathcal O_E)_Y$ and the completed sheaf is asserted.

source.place: constant-section construction in the missing integral-linearity justification; limits as in the cited definition

proof.text: Put $\mathcal O=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. On morphisms $f:M\to N$ of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves set $(a f)_U(x)=c_U(a)f_U(x)$. Each $A_{E,n}$ is commutative; local representatives in its constant sheaf therefore commute, and multiplication in their inverse limit is coordinatewise. Hence $\mathcal O$ is commutative, so $(a f)_U$ is $\mathcal O(U)$-linear. Semilinearity of restriction and $c_U(a)|_V=c_V(a)$ show that these components commute with restriction. All module identities hold sectionwise: $(a+b)f=af+bf$, $a(f+g)=af+ag$, $(ab)f=a(bf)$ and $1f=f$. For composable $f,g$, linearity of $g_U$ gives $g_U(c_U(a)f_U(x))=c_U(a)g_U(f_U(x))$, hence $g\circ(af)=a(g\circ f)=(ag)\circ f$. Addition is sectionwise as well. Thus the sheaf category is $\mathcal O_E$-linear; its abelian structure is supplied by the cited module-category statement in a universe large enough for the site.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category with $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $\mathcal A=\Mod(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$, using the abelian category and scalar action of Step 3. The derived category here is exactly $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ by the completed-coefficients definition. Take the localization universe from the abstract-derived-category convention. The lemma makes this category linear, its localization functor linear, and every integer shift linear. To identify the action, multiplication by $c_U(a)$ on each term defines a cochain endomorphism $\mu_{a,K}$, since the differentials are module maps; already on complexes $\mu_{a,K}=a\,\mathrm{id}_K$. Consequently $Q(\mu_{a,K})=a\,\mathrm{id}_{QK}$. For any derived morphism $f:QK\to QL$, bilinearity now gives $af=Q(\mu_{a,L})\circ f=f\circ Q(\mu_{a,K})$. Thus it is exactly the action through the constant global sections constructed above, including on morphisms introduced by localization.

By def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ is a full subcategory of the ambient derived category. Give each of its Hom groups exactly the ambient module structure: sums, scalar multiples and compositions still have the same source and target, so all module and bilinearity identities are the ambient identities. By lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated it is closed under every integer shift and has the induced triangulated structure. Its shift maps on Hom groups are therefore the ambient shift maps, and $[m](af)=a[m](f)$ is the identity proved in Step 4. This proves the final assertion without imposing a new boundedness, finite-Tor-dimension, or coefficient hypothesis.
